title: UC1 · AWS · Taiwan digital bank: cell-based core APIs and real-time fraud MLOps on EKS
prompt:
Design the AWS architecture for a Taiwan digital bank that runs its customer-facing banking APIs and a real-time fraud-scoring ML model on Amazon EKS. The bank is regulated by the Taiwan FSC and the networking team enforces very strict controls. Draw one diagram that shows all of the following.

REGIONS AND HA
1. Primary region: AWS Asia Pacific (Taipei) ap-east-2, using 3 Availability Zones. DR region: Asia Pacific (Tokyo) ap-northeast-1 in warm standby. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database across the two regions. Use Route 53 Application Recovery Controller for the regional failover decision. Targets are RPO under 1 minute and RTO under 15 minutes.
2. Use a cell-based architecture. Each cell is its own AWS account and VPC, with its own EKS cluster, Aurora cluster and ElastiCache, and serves a bounded set of customers. A thin cell router places each customer in a cell: CloudFront Functions with a CloudFront KeyValueStore map from customer ID to cell. Show at least 2 cells in Taipei and the standby cells in Tokyo.

NETWORKING (strict)
3. Hybrid connectivity from the on-prem data center: 2 AWS Direct Connect locations with 2 dedicated connections each (maximum resiliency model, MACsec) into a Direct Connect Gateway, with a transit VIF to an AWS Transit Gateway in each region. Add an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet, attached to the TGW, as backup; DX is preferred through BGP.
4. Use a centralized network account. The TGW has separate route tables for prod, non-prod and shared services. An inspection VPC runs AWS Network Firewall with TGW appliance mode, and every east-west and north-south flow passes through it. A central egress VPC uses NAT Gateway plus a Network Firewall domain allow-list. Workload VPCs have no Internet Gateway and no NAT.
5. Internet ingress goes through Route 53, then CloudFront with AWS WAF and Shield Advanced, then CloudFront VPC origins to an INTERNAL Application Load Balancer in each cell. There is no public ALB anywhere.
6. Partner fintechs call the bank's APIs only over AWS PrivateLink (a VPC endpoint service backed by an NLB). Branch and back-office users reach internal APIs over DX through the TGW. Use Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints for hybrid DNS.
7. All AWS service access uses VPC endpoints: interface endpoints for ECR, STS, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs and SageMaker Runtime, and a gateway endpoint for S3. Endpoint policies restrict access to the organization.

COMPUTE AND MLOPS
8. Each cell runs a private EKS cluster (private API endpoint only) across 3 AZs. It uses Karpenter plus HPA for autoscaling, the AWS Load Balancer Controller, VPC CNI security groups for pods, Kubernetes network policies and EKS Pod Identity.
9. Shared-services ML account: a training EKS cluster with Kubeflow Pipelines and MLflow, GPU Karpenter node pools on Spot, S3 for the feature and model store, and an MLflow model registry. Argo CD deploys approved models into each cell as a canary, one cell at a time. Transaction events stream through Amazon MSK (private) to an online feature store on ElastiCache.
10. Performance target: fraud scoring p99 under 100 ms at 5,000 TPS per cell.

IDENTITY AND GOVERNANCE
11. AWS Organizations with OUs (Security, Network, Shared Services, Workloads-Prod, Workloads-NonProd). IAM Identity Center is federated with the corporate IdP. SCPs deny regions other than ap-east-2 and ap-northeast-1, deny creating Internet Gateways in workload accounts, and deny disabling CloudTrail. Use permission boundaries, EKS access entries and KMS customer-managed keys.
12. Security and audit: an organization CloudTrail to a Log Archive account, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty, Security Hub and AWS Config.

Note any service that should be verified for regional availability in ap-east-2.

title: UC2 · Azure · Electronics manufacturer: hybrid factory-to-cloud visual-inspection MLOps on AKS
prompt:
Create an Azure architecture diagram, using Azure icons, for a Taiwan electronics manufacturer. Factories in Hsinchu, Taichung and Vietnam run AI visual defect inspection. Models are trained in Azure and served both in Azure and at the factory edge. The OT/IT network team requires that NOTHING is reachable from the public internet except one supplier portal, and that all PaaS traffic stays private. Draw one diagram that shows all of the following.

REGIONS AND HA
1. Primary region: Japan East. Secondary region: Southeast Asia. Run active-active for the inference and MES APIs. (The Azure Taiwan North region is not generally available yet, so do not use it.)
2. Use the Deployment Stamps (cell) pattern. Each stamp holds a group of factories and has its own AKS cluster, Event Hubs namespace and Cosmos DB container. Show 2 stamps per region. A global routing layer maps each factory to its stamp.

NETWORKING (strict)
3. Azure Virtual WAN with a secured hub in each region (Azure Firewall Premium with TLS inspection and IDPS, and routing intent for private and internet traffic). Use landing-zone spoke VNets.
4. Hybrid connectivity: 2 ExpressRoute circuits from the Taipei HQ data center at 2 different peering locations, connected to both hubs. ExpressRoute Global Reach links the Taiwan factories. The Vietnam factory connects with Site-to-Site VPN (active-active, BGP) to the vWAN VPN gateway, and HQ uses S2S VPN as the ExpressRoute backup.
5. Use Private Endpoints for the Azure ML workspace, ACR (Premium, geo-replicated), Storage/ADLS Gen2, Key Vault, Cosmos DB and Event Hubs. Use Private DNS zones linked to the hubs, and Azure DNS Private Resolver for on-prem conditional forwarding. Public network access is disabled on all PaaS.
6. Ingress: internal MES users come over ExpressRoute to an internal Application Gateway WAF v2 with a private frontend only. The single supplier portal is published through Azure Front Door Premium with WAF, using a Private Link origin (Private Link Service on the AKS internal load balancer). There are no public IPs in any spoke.
7. Egress: AKS uses outboundType userDefinedRouting through the hub Azure Firewall with an FQDN allow-list.

COMPUTE AND MLOPS
8. AKS is a private cluster with Azure CNI Overlay and Cilium network policy, Workload Identity, the cluster autoscaler plus KEDA, a system node pool, and a GPU user node pool across 3 availability zones.
9. Azure Machine Learning uses a managed VNet in 'allow only approved outbound' mode. Pipelines train on low-priority GPU compute clusters, use an MLflow model registry, and use an Azure ML Registry to replicate models across both regions. Models deploy to AKS through GitOps (Flux) with a canary rollout.
10. Edge: at each factory, an Azure Arc-enabled AKS edge cluster runs inference with p99 latency under 50 ms per camera frame. It pulls images from an ACR connected registry over ExpressRoute. Inspection images and labels flow back to ADLS Gen2 for retraining.

IDENTITY AND GOVERNANCE
11. Microsoft Entra ID with PIM (just-in-time) and Conditional Access. Use managed identities everywhere. Management groups follow the Cloud Adoption Framework landing zone layout. Azure Policy denies public IPs and public network access. Use Defender for Cloud, Log Analytics and Azure Monitor.

title: UC3 · GCP · Omnichannel retailer: multi-region GKE commerce and recommendation MLOps
prompt:
Create a Google Cloud architecture diagram, using Google Cloud icons, for a Taiwan omnichannel retailer. The retailer has 3,000 stores and an e-commerce app, and runs real-time product recommendation and demand-forecasting ML. Security requires private-only service access and data-exfiltration protection. Draw one diagram that shows all of the following.

REGIONS AND HA
1. Run active-active in asia-east1 (Changhua County, Taiwan) and asia-northeast1 (Tokyo), each with 3 zones. Use a globally consistent database for orders and inventory that spans both regions (Cloud Spanner multi-region, or explain your alternative). Memorystore for Redis is the regional cache.
2. Use a cell-based architecture. Each region has 2 regional GKE cells, and each cell serves a shard of stores and customers. Cell routing is done at the global load balancer with URL map and header-based routing, using a cell-assignment service. A cell failure must affect only its own shard.

NETWORKING (strict)
3. Use Shared VPC host projects (prod and non-prod) with service projects per team. Use hierarchical firewall policies and Cloud NGFW Enterprise (IPS).
4. Hybrid connectivity: Dedicated Interconnect in the 99.99% topology (4 connections across 2 metros, with Cloud Routers in both regions) from the HQ and distribution-center data centers. The 3,000 stores connect through HA VPN from SD-WAN appliances, terminated as Network Connectivity Center hybrid spokes on an NCC hub.
5. Use Private Service Connect: a PSC endpoint for Google APIs (vpc-sc bundle), PSC endpoints for Vertex AI online prediction, and a PSC published service so the payment-gateway partner can reach the order API privately. Use Cloud DNS private zones with inbound and outbound server policies for hybrid DNS.
6. A VPC Service Controls perimeter covers Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Storage and Artifact Registry, with access levels for on-prem ranges. Egress goes through Cloud NAT and Secure Web Proxy with a URL allow-list. GKE nodes have no external IPs.
7. Ingress: e-commerce traffic goes through the Global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud Armor (WAF and Adaptive Protection) and Cloud CDN, then through a GKE multi-cluster Gateway to the cells. Store POS APIs go through a cross-region internal Application Load Balancer that is reachable only over Interconnect or HA VPN.

COMPUTE AND MLOPS
8. GKE Enterprise regional private clusters: private control-plane endpoint, Dataplane V2 network policy, Workload Identity Federation for GKE, cluster autoscaler with node auto-provisioning, HPA, and L4 GPU node pools for low-latency recommendation serving (p95 under 80 ms).
9. MLOps: POS and clickstream data flow through Pub/Sub and Dataflow into BigQuery. Vertex AI Pipelines train demand-forecast and recommendation models, with Vertex AI Feature Store backed by BigQuery and the Vertex AI Model Registry. Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy promote models and services to the GKE cells one cell at a time (canary), with Binary Authorization. Vertex AI Model Monitoring triggers retraining.

IDENTITY AND GOVERNANCE
10. Use Cloud Identity federated with the corporate IdP, a resource hierarchy of organization, then folders (prod, non-prod, shared), then projects, and IAM Deny policies. Organization Policy constraints restrict resource locations to asia-east1 and asia-northeast1, restrict external IPs, and disable service-account key creation. Use Privileged Access Manager for just-in-time access. Use Cloud KMS CMEK, Cloud Audit Logs to a central logging project, and Security Command Center.
